text.p: A senior Genzyme Corp executive said on Thursday the company was comfortable with Wall Street forecasts for its 1996 earnings in the $1.05 to $1.10 range.

"I think the $1.05-$1.10 range is pretty much right on," Genzyme senior vice president Gregory Phelps told reporters following a presentation at a biotechnology conference organized by The Carson Group and BioCentury Publications.

He estimated Genzyme's 1996 revenues at about $500 million, of which $20-$25 million would come from research and development revenues. Deknatel Snowden Pencer, a surgical company acquired by Genzyme in July, would contribute about $50 million in the second half, he said.
First Call listed the consensus of analysts' estimates for Genzyme's earnings in 1996 at $1.11 a share, versus $0.97 in 1995.
